description: Customers' agents create, route, assign, and answer tickets in the agent workspace; the core of the subscription
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Core SLA component: credits start after 22 minutes (Enterprise) and 43 minutes (Standard) and step up at 3.6 hours; 4 hours triggers bank customer notice (12 CFR 53.4); about 79,000 tickets an hour stop moving
manual_workaround: Status page and customer email updates; customers fall back to shared inboxes and phone; no company-side manual workaround for the service itself
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; content delivery and WAF provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Platform engineering and site reliability on-call; support leadership
quantified_operational_impact: About 79,000 tickets an hour across 2,400 customers and 88,000 agents are blocked
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Full SLA credit step at 4 hours (10% Enterprise, 10% Standard); 9 bank customers notified at 4 hours (12 CFR 53.4); 38 Enterprise customers expect status within 24 hours

description: Real-time chat widget, in-app messaging, and social messaging conversations between end consumers and agents
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Core SLA component for the about 70% of customers that use chat; conversations are real time, so an outage is immediately visible to end consumers
manual_workaround: Chat widget shows an offline form that creates email tickets (works if ingestion is up)
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; social messaging connector provider
quantified_operational_impact: About 27,000 chat conversations an hour are dropped or converted to offline messages
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: SLA credits for the affected 70% of revenue; Enterprise contact-center customers may claim chat-specific service levels

description: Inbound email, web forms, and social messages become tickets
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Core SLA component; senders' mail servers retry delivery, so little data is lost, but tickets arrive late and customers see backlogs
manual_workaround: Email providers queue and retry; customers can read their support mailboxes directly
dependent_third_parties: Email delivery service; cloud provider A
quantified_operational_impact: About 52,000 inbound emails an hour queue upstream; backlog clears in about 2 hours after recovery
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: SLA credits for all customers (ingestion is in the core service definition)

description: Customer systems create and update tickets through the API; webhooks push events to customer systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Core SLA component; about 65% of customers integrate order and CRM systems; failed webhooks must be replayed
manual_workaround: Customers queue API calls and retry; webhook replay after recovery
quantified_operational_impact: About 140,000 API calls a minute at peak fail; webhook backlog must be replayed in order
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: SLA credits for the affected 65% of revenue

description: Ticketing, messaging, and AI Assist for 46 healthcare customers in the separate healthcare production account
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same service levels as Enterprise; patients use it to reach clinics and telehealth providers; the BAA requires the company to protect the availability of ePHI (45 CFR 164.306(a)(1))
manual_workaround: Clinics revert to phone lines and their patient portals; status page; direct calls from customer success to each of the 46 customers
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; email delivery service; SMS provider; AI model provider (zero-retention endpoint)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Platform engineering on-call; healthcare customer success team
quantified_operational_impact: About 1.3 million patients' records; about 40,000 patient messages a day are delayed
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: HIPAA availability safeguards as a business associate (contingency plan, 164.308(a)(7)); SLA credits on $0.5 million a month

description: Public help center pages and articles that end consumers use for self-service
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Not in the SLA; when the help center is down, ticket volume rises about 15% because self-service deflection stops
manual_workaround: Customers post a banner on their own sites; articles cached at the content delivery network for up to 1 hour
quantified_operational_impact: About 3 million help center page views a day; about 15% more tickets while down

business_process: AI features (AI Assist and Answer Bot)
description: Generative AI reply drafting for agents and the customer-facing Answer Bot
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Not in the core SLA; the AI add-on is billed per resolution (about $25,000 a day); agents can answer without drafts
manual_workaround: Feature flag off; agents reply manually; Answer Bot falls back to the contact form
quantified_operational_impact: About 210,000 AI drafts and 18,000 Answer Bot conversations a day stop
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: AI add-on revenue lost for the outage; no regulatory deadline

description: In-product dashboards on ticket volume, response times, and satisfaction
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Reports can be regenerated from the database; customers use them weekly
manual_workaround: Customers export raw data through the API

description: SIEM, MDR monitoring, detection engineering, and incident handling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Notice clocks keep running when monitoring is down: 24 to 48 hours to customers, 10 business days under BAAs, 4 hours for bank customers; losing logs prevents scoping
manual_workaround: MDR provider monitors from its own platform; cloud provider native alerts; manual review of cloud audit logs
dependent_third_parties: MDR provider; SIEM provider; cloud provider A
quantified_operational_impact: Detection gap for the platform and endpoints; investigation cannot scope affected tenants
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Missed or late customer, BAA, and bank notices; inability to show reasonable security (FTC Act Section 5)

description: Build, test, sign, and deploy code and infrastructure changes; also the path for emergency fixes
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No customer-facing impact while production runs, but emergency fixes during an incident depend on it; 190 engineers blocked
manual_workaround: Break-glass deploy procedure from a signed artifact with two-person approval
quantified_operational_impact: About 40 deployments a day stop; engineering time lost
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: SOC 2 change management evidence must cover any break-glass deploy (Type 2 exception 2)

description: The company's own support team answers customer questions and incident updates; runs on the company's own platform
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers need updates during platform incidents; if the platform is down, the support desk is down too
manual_workaround: Backup support mailbox at the email delivery service; status page; customer success managers call top accounts
dependent_third_parties: Status page provider; email delivery service
quantified_operational_impact: About 3,500 support tickets a day from customers
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Enterprise contracts require incident status updates

business_process: Customer onboarding, implementation, and data migration
description: Tenant setup, data imports from prior systems, and professional services projects
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Go-live dates can slip a few days; imports can be rerun
manual_workaround: Reschedule go-lives; rerun imports from customer exports
dependent_people_or_facilities: 70 customer success and professional services staff
quantified_operational_impact: About 25 implementations in flight at any time

business_process: Billing, invoicing, collections, and service credit processing
description: Monthly subscription invoices, usage billing for AI resolutions, collections, and SLA credit calculation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly billing run; a delay of several days slips about $8.33 million of invoices but loses little
manual_workaround: Run invoices from the prior month's billing data; manual credit memos
quantified_operational_impact: Invoices for about $8.33 million a month delayed
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Credit calculations must be accurate for SLA claims

description: CRM pipeline, quotes, renewals, and answers to customer security questionnaires
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Deals slip but are rarely lost in 3 days; questionnaire answers come from the trust center library
manual_workaround: Work from exported pipeline reports and the trust center library
quantified_operational_impact: About 60 renewals and 40 new deals a month
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Questionnaire answers are representations (FTC Act Section 5); see P03

description: Workforce single sign-on, MFA, email, chat, and laptops; needed to operate and recover everything else
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without the identity provider nobody can reach the cloud console, CI/CD, or support tools, which blocks recovery of BP-01 to BP-11
manual_workaround: Sealed break-glass accounts for the cloud organization and identity provider; out-of-band incident bridge on personal phones
dependent_third_parties: Identity provider vendor; productivity suite provider
quantified_operational_impact: 600 staff blocked; recovery of the platform cannot start
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Recovery of every SLA process depends on it

description: Payroll, benefits, onboarding and offboarding, contractor records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; offboarding delays leave access open (Type 2 exception 1)
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll provider; manual offboarding checklist to the Director of IT
quantified_regulatory_or_contractual_imp: Late offboarding is a SOC 2 exception and a HIPAA termination procedure issue (164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C))

description: Product usage analytics, revenue reporting, and board metrics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Board and sponsor reporting is monthly; the warehouse can be reloaded from sources
manual_workaround: Use billing system reports for urgent requests
dependent_third_parties: Data platform on cloud provider B
